verdict.rationale: skills.sh is a skills registry and CLI. A tool of this kind could plausibly ship a built-in assistant, so the axis applies, but the evidence shows none. The closest feature, `skills use --agent`, launches an external third-party coding agent (e.g. Claude Code) with a generated prompt. That is handing off to another product's agent, not delegating to an assistant built into skills.sh, so it earns no credit.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product
